mechanism: selective safety certification for first-output TTFT under guaranteed Decode-stage overlap risk
motivation: Fresh HELIX stage tracing showed that the high-load TTFT miss is almost entirely load-dependent compute-node residence during the first Decode token; source wait and link time do not increase. Instantaneous concurrency, remaining current-token work, phase dispersion, and remaining decode lifetime are useful risk signals but are not accurate enough to become additive latency formulas.

guard.primary: If the unmodified J1 evaluator says safe, abstain from certifying safe when any request's profile-driven first-Decode interval contains more active Decode requests than the number of pipeline stages.
guard.structural_threshold: strictly greater than K, where K=len(pipeline.stages); K is not fitted from outcomes.
guard.secondary_diagnostic_only: also report >=K to show the coverage/conservatism sensitivity, but do not select it from this back-check.
guard.fallback: uncertain points require execution-reference validation or a future stronger compute-contention model; they are not counted as certified safe.

model_guardrails.J1_latency_semantics: unchanged standard first-output TTFT and request-average post-first TPOT

populations.short_confirmation: h103 and h105 formal workloads; 528 cached conditions
populations.long_confirmation: h104 and h106 formal workloads; 490 cached conditions

metrics: false certified-safe count among reference-unsafe points
binary-equivalent false rejection if uncertain were treated as unsafe
success_rule: Primary >K guard is useful only if it removes the known unsafe certifications on the design back-check and does not create unsafe certified-safe cases on the two confirmation populations. Coverage loss must be reported rather than hidden.
